title: Right shifts of the specified completed integral tensor product
statement:
Fix a prime $\ell$, a finite extension $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$ with valuation ring $R=\mathcal O_E$ and uniformizer $\varpi$, and put $A_n=R/\varpi^n$ for $n\geq1$. Let $W$ be a scheme on which $\ell$ is invertible. Use the small pro-etale site and the completed coefficient sheaf $B=\widehat{\mathcal O}_{E,W}=\varprojlim_n(A_n)_W$ of [def-pur-integral-derived-operations]. For objects $M,N$ of the ambient derived category $D(W_{\mathrm{proet}},\mathcal O_E)=D(B)$ of $B$-module sheaves, use the completed tensor $\widehat\otimes^L_R$ constructed in [def-pur-integral-derived-operations] by the functorial complex $\operatorname{Cone}(1-s)[-1]$ of the finite-reduction tensor tower, with the total tensor convention of [def-pc-tensor-complex-sheaves]. For each integer $r$ there is an isomorphism, natural in $M,N$,
$$
\sigma^r_{M,N}:M\widehat\otimes^L_R(N[r])\xrightarrow{\sim}(M\widehat\otimes^L_RN)[r].
$$
Here $C[r]^j=C^{j+r}$ and $d_{C[r]}=(-1)^r d_C$. The isomorphism is independent of the chosen flat-term K-flat resolutions. On such resolutions $P,Q$, its finite-level tensor comparison sends the summand $P_n^i\otimes Q_n^{j+r}$ to the corresponding summand of $\operatorname{Tot}(P_n\otimes Q_n)[r]$ by multiplication by $(-1)^{ri}$. These comparisons commute with the quotient transition maps in the reduction tower. On the product mapping-fiber model they induce the displayed isomorphism using the degreewise product shift identification and the cone comparison $\operatorname{Cone}(f[r])\to\operatorname{Cone}(f)[r]$, $(b,a)\mapsto(b,(-1)^r a)$, for the convention $\operatorname{Cone}(f)=B'\oplus A'[1]$ when $f:A'\to B'$.

proof.text: First work with arbitrary complexes $U,V$ of sheaves of modules over a commutative ring sheaf. Set $S_r(U,V):\operatorname{Tot}(U\otimes V[r])\to\operatorname{Tot}(U\otimes V)[r]$ to multiply the summand $U^i\otimes V^{j+r}$, where $i+j=k$, by $(-1)^{ri}$. By [def-pc-tensor-complex-sheaves], the source differential has components $d_U\otimes1$ and $(-1)^{i+r}1\otimes d_V$, while the target differential is $(-1)^r(d_U\otimes1+(-1)^i1\otimes d_V)$. For the first component, $S_rd$ has coefficient $(-1)^{r(i+1)}=(-1)^{ri+r}$, equal to that of $dS_r$. For the second, both coefficients are $(-1)^{ri+i+r}$. These equations on each direct-sum inclusion prove the chain-map identity. The same sign gives its inverse. Every degree-zero map preserves $i$, so these maps are natural in $U,V$.

Choose flat-term K-flat resolutions $P\to M$ and $Q\to N$ by [lem-pc-kflat-resolution] on the ringed site $(W_{\mathrm{proet}},B)$ of [def-pur-integral-derived-operations]. The complex $Q[r]$ still has flat terms, and is K-flat: for any acyclic $F$, step 1 identifies $\operatorname{Tot}(F\otimes Q[r])$ with $\operatorname{Tot}(F\otimes Q)[r]$, which is acyclic by [def-pc-kflat-complex] since shifting only reindexes kernels and images and multiplies differentials by a unit. The shifted augmentation $Q[r]\to N[r]$ is a quasi-isomorphism by the same cohomology calculation. Hence $P,Q[r]$ are permissible models for the completed tensor on the left.

Reduction is termwise tensor with $(A_n)_W$, so $(Q[r])_n=Q_n[r]$ with its signed differential. Write $C_n=\operatorname{Res}_n\operatorname{Tot}(P_n\otimes Q_n)$ and $D_n=\operatorname{Res}_n\operatorname{Tot}(P_n\otimes Q_n[r])$ as in [def-pur-integral-derived-operations]. Step 1 gives $\alpha_n:D_n\xrightarrow{\sim}C_n[r]$. The transition map is induced by the quotient maps on $P_n,Q_n$; each is degree zero, so it preserves $i$ and commutes with $(-1)^{ri}$. Thus $\alpha_n t^D_n=t^C_n[r]\alpha_{n+1}$. This is an actual isomorphism of towers of $B$-module complexes, before passing to the derived category.

For any tower $C_\bullet$, put $X=\prod_n C_n$ and $f=1-s:X\to X$. The degreewise identification $\prod_n(C_n[r])\cong X[r]$ commutes with differentials, since both use $(-1)^rd$, and identifies $1-s$ with $f[r]$. Use the cone convention stated in [def-weil-abstract-derived-category], $d_{\operatorname{Cone}(f)}(b,a)=(db+f(a),-da)$. The map $h_r:\operatorname{Cone}(f[r])\to\operatorname{Cone}(f)[r]$, $(b,a)\mapsto(b,(-1)^ra)$, is a chain isomorphism: both $h_rd$ and $dh_r$ give $((-1)^r db+f(a),-da)$, with inverse the same diagonal sign. These equations are natural in commuting squares of chain maps. Shifting $h_r$ by $[-1]$ and identifying $[r][-1]=[-1][r]$ gives $\operatorname{Rlim}^{\mathrm c}(C_\bullet[r])\cong\operatorname{Rlim}^{\mathrm c}(C_\bullet)[r]$ for the functorial mapping-fiber construction in [def-pur-integral-derived-operations].

proof.text: Apply the product and cone functors to the commuting tower isomorphism $\alpha$ of step 3, obtaining $\operatorname{Rlim}^{\mathrm c}(D_\bullet)\xrightarrow{\sim}\operatorname{Rlim}^{\mathrm c}(C_\bullet[r])$. Compose with step 4. By [def-pur-integral-derived-operations], the source computes $M\widehat\otimes_R^L(N[r])$ and the final target computes $(M\widehat\otimes_R^L N)[r]$. This composite is the asserted $\sigma^r$ on the chosen resolutions, with exactly the finite-level formula, reduction-transition compatibility, product identification, and cone comparison in the statement. All component maps are chain isomorphisms, so the composite is an isomorphism.

proof.text: The chain formulas in steps 1–5 commute with every map of flat-term K-flat representatives. By [lem-pur-integral-operations-well-defined](1), their completed tensor constructions send quasi-isomorphisms between such representatives to quasi-isomorphisms; by (2) they descend to functors on $D(B)^2$ with natural comparison isomorphisms on K-flat representatives. A commuting naturality square with a quasi-isomorphism remains commuting after inverting that map. Hence the same squares commute for all composites and inverses that define the localized functors of (2). They therefore give a natural isomorphism on $D(B)^2$. The unique comparison isomorphisms of functors in (2) commute with this isomorphism, since their components are induced by these same localized comparisons. This proves independence of the resolution choices in the comparison-compatible sense of that node, as well as naturality in arbitrary derived morphisms of $M,N$.

reviewed.note: mechanical checks by tools/merge_delivery.py; mathematics reviewed in full by NT-cc-N9-34684d277 (reviewer sub-agent of L); spot-checked: I read the delivery in full, recomputed every sign identity by hand and made no changes. The delivery splits the existing item into six steps and creates no new node. The statement uses the coefficient category D(W_proet,O_E)=D(B) and the completed tensor Rlim^c Res_n Tot(P_n⊗Q_n) exactly as def-pur-integral-derived-operations defines them, and does not identify it with the Bhatt–Scholze derived-completion tensor. The shift and cone conventions match def-weil-abstract-derived-category. Step 1: the Koszul sign (-1)^{ri} makes a chain map; both components (-1)^{ri+r} and (-1)^{ri+i+r} agree under the Tot convention of def-pc-tensor-complex-sheaves. Step 2: Q[r] is K-flat with flat terms by step 1 and the definition in def-pc-kflat-complex, and resolutions exist by lem-pc-kflat-resolution. Step 3: the transition maps have degree 0, so the towers are isomorphic on the nose. Step 4: h_r(b,a)=(b,(-1)^r a) is a chain isomorphism; both sides equal ((-1)^r db+fa,-da), and [r][-1]=[-1][r] holds exactly. Step 5: composing steps 3 and 4 gives the map. Step 6: naturality on D(B)^2 and resolution independence follow from lem-pur-integral-operations-well-defined clauses (1) and (2), used for what they state. Test cases r=0, r=1 and a one-term complex all check out. Sources: Bhatt–Scholze Definition 3.4.10 and Lemma 3.4.12(4) on pp. 22–23, Stacks tags 011G, 012Z, 014E, 08TC, 06YS and 06YT, and the last sentence of the blueprint main-20261015 lem-sf-twist-interchange proof. No SGA is cited. No duplicate exists: the existing shift nodes are about D(O_X) or ring-level tensors. Accepted tool_uses: lem-pc-kflat-resolution and lem-pur-integral-operations-well-defined; the three cited definitions are notions, so declaring them is harmless.
